newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Japan, S.Korea to boost defence ties against North.
newsitem.headline: Japan, S.Korea to boost defence ties against North.

text.p: Japan and South Korea agreed on Monday to coordinate their defence policies to counter threats posed by North Korea, a Seoul defence ministry spokesman said.
The agreement was reached in a meeting between Japanese Defence Minister Fumio Kyuma and his South Korean counterpart Kim Dong-jin.
"The two ministers shared the view that North Korea had weapons of mass destruction that threaten peace on the Korean peninsula and the region," the spokesman said.

"They agreed to closely cooperate in security policies to deal with North Korea. Minister Kyuma reaffirmed Japan's support for four-way peace talks and agreed to seek joint steps on the matter," he added.

Seoul does not want its allies to offer large-scale economic assistance to Pyongyang until it agrees to join talks aimed at securing a lasting peace to replace a truce agreement that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
The four-nation talks would involve the two Koreas, the United States and China.
North Korea has signalled it is seeking massive food aid, diplomatic recognition from Washington and an easing of the U.S.-imposed trade embargo before joining the talks.
Japan has held back food aid to North Korea, partly due to public anger over charges that North Korea kidnapped a Japanese schoolgirl in 1977 and spirited her to Pyongyang.
Impending famine is shaking hopes of coaxing North Korea towards a "soft landing" -- a slow reform of its system leading to peaceful unification with the South over several decades.
Officials in Seoul, Tokyo and Washington have expressed fears that a desperate North Korea might strike the South if its economic crisis threatened its Stalinist system.

A high-ranking North Korean defector, Hwang Jang-yop, was quoted last week in a Seoul daily as saying North Korea could turn the capitalist South into a "sea of flames" and scorch Japan in a nuclear attack if the United States tried to intervene.
